subject: Assurance on model-training usage and retention windows — Q&A
messages:
From: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@clearbridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@clearbridge.com>, procurement@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-10-21 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on 'not used to train' language and retention TTLs

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearBridge is keen to move forward. Before procurement signs off we need a clear, written confirmation on two items:

1) Your platform statement: "we do not use customer content to train models." Can you confirm exactly what that covers (logs, prompts, embeddings, support transcripts, telemetry)? Is any aggregated or anonymized data used for model tuning?

2) Retention / deletion windows: what are standard TTLs for different artifacts (request payloads, KV cache/prefix caching, backups/snapshots, logs)? If we require a shorter window and an attestation that data is deleted, what is the timeline and process?

Can you share an attestation doc and a short summary for procurement? We need something we can attach to the SOW.

Appreciate a concise reply — procurement would like to close this week.

Best,
Jennifer
Director, Security & Compliance
ClearBridge Finance

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@clearbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on 'not used to train' language and retention TTLs

Hi Jennifer — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details below and attachments.

TL;DR
- Redwood does not use customer prompt/content to train public models by default. We offer an explicit "no-train" attestation and can enforce technical controls per account.
- Aggregated, product-telemetry (non-identifying) may be used to improve platform reliability unless specifically opted out.
- Default retention windows: ephemeral request payloads (7 days by default), logs & telemetry (90–180 days depending on retention tier), backups/snapshots (configurable; default 90 days). We can reduce those in contract or for Private deployments.

Details:
1) "Do not train" scope: request payloads, generated responses, uploaded files, and embeddings tied to your tenant are not pulled into model training datasets when the account is configured with the no-train flag. That flag applies across hosted and dedicated tenants.

2) Telemetry vs content: we distinguish customer content (prompts, files) from platform telemetry (latency metrics, error rates, anonymized usage counts). Telemetry is used internally to improve runtime behavior (scheduling, batching heuristics) but not for model parameter updates unless a customer explicitly opts into product improvement programs.

3) Backups & snapshots: we retain periodic snapshots for recovery. Snapshot retention is a configurable policy. Default: 90 days. We can set snapshot TTLs to 30/14/0 days in contract for strict customers; for Private deployments snapshots stay in-customer VPC and never leave unless requested.

4) Deletion and attestation: for hosted accounts we implement a tombstone + purge workflow. After a deletion request we mark data for purge immediately and run background erasure jobs; full removal from backups/snapshots is targeted within 30 days by default (can be shortened to 7–14 days under an agreement). We will provide an attestation PDF after purge completion.

5) Edge cases: debug traces and ephemeral KV caches may persist short periods to preserve request-level latency guarantees; we treat those as ephemeral and include them in the deletion/purge window.

I'll attach our no-train attestation and a short retention-options spreadsheet for procurement. Marissa is looping in procurement language options.

If you want, Priyom from Trust & Safety can add a short technical note on KV-cache and snapshot eradication steps.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Trust & Safety Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_no-train_attestation_v2.pdf, retention-options-summary.xlsx

Thanks, Irene — that helps. A couple follow-ups:

- Can you confirm "telemetry" will never be fed into model training even in aggregate unless we opt in? Some legal teams treat "aggregate" as still problematic.
- For snapshots: does the 30-day purge timeline include offsite backups / cloud provider backups (snapshots stored in object storage)? We need confirmation that provider-level backups are handled in the 30-day window.

Also procurement would like a draft clause to add to the MA that locks in no-train + 30-day purge for content and 90-day telemetry retention (unless we choose the stricter 30-day option).

-Jennifer

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-22 15:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on 'not used to train' language and retention TTLs

Hi all — quick technical clarifications to support the legal language.

1) Snapshots and cloud-provider persistence: our snapshot process writes encrypted objects to a customer-dedicated prefix in object storage. The TTL we enforce is application-level: when we purge we issue deletes for the snapshot objects and for any provider-level lifecycle objects. In practice providers may have eventual consistency; our SLA for object deletion is 30 days by default, 14 days under special agreement. We will produce a deletion manifest for audit.

2) KV/prefix caches: these are in-memory or local-disk caches on serving nodes and are not part of persistent training datasets. They are included in the ephemeral category and are scrubbed on node termination; we also run a background scrub cycle.

3) Telemetry: only non-identifying, aggregated telemetry is used for runtime improvements. Model-parameter training is off-limits unless you sign a separate data contribution/opt-in.

4) Evidence: after a purge we can provide a signed attestation and a manifest listing purged object ids (or a redacted manifest for security). For private deployments we can provide exportable audit logs showing no egress.

If helpful I can share the internal runbook (redacted) that shows purge job steps and checks.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Manager, Trust & Safety Engineering
Redwood Inference
